To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Weaver down-converter can achieve high image rejection ratios and the image rejection can also be further improved by generating coherent LO signals.

the Weaver architecture can be implemented using GaInP/GAs HBTs to achieve a high image rejection ratio and the image rejection ratio of the Weaver architecture can further be improved by making the two LO signals coherent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the image rejection down-converter using GaInP/Gas HBT technology.
the design of a GaInP/GaN HBT Weaver down-converter for wireless applications.
the design and analysis of the Weaver image rejection down-converter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is a very important and useful contribution to the literature on Weaver down-converters.
the proposed down-converter is a promising candidate for the future wireless communications.
the Weaver architecture can be used as a good image rejection down-converter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the image rejection ratio of a Weaver system is mainly determined by the phase difference of LO1 and LO 2.
the Weaver down-converter is a good candidate for low cost, low power and high image rejection applications.
a GaInP/GGaAs heterojunction-bipolar-transistor (HBT) image-rejection down-converter with the Weaver architecture is successfully demonstrated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new Weaver down-converter architecture can be designed to have the image rejection ratios better than 40 dB when the LO frequency is higher than 10 GHz.
the LO frequency quadrupler can be used to generate the LO signals for a down-converter and the image rejection ratio of the down-converter is improved.
the Weaver architecture can be used to design high image rejection down-converters with a low LO frequency.
